parsed.summary: The design files match the specification in all checked areas: power paths, jumper-selectable PWM/serial servo routing, MAX3485 auto-direction circuit, component values, and connector pin assignments. No deviation that would change board behavior was found.

response.reasoning:
We need answer JSON only. Need review design files against spec. Need determine anomaly. Let's inspect thoroughly.

We have netlist. Need find deviations. Spec describes intended design. We need identify anomaly if any. Let's parse.

Components:
C1-C4 100u on servo rail downstream D2: Net-(D2-K) to GND. Check C3 pin1 on Net-(D2-K), pin2 GND yes. C1 pin2 Net(D2-K), pin1 GND; C2 pin2 Net, pin1 GND; C4 pin2 Net, pin1 GND. Okay polarity not relevant.

J1/J2 2x15 pass-through. Nets mostly identical. Need compare with spec: J1/J2 identical nets on both. Check net assignments. J1 pin1 /PIN1, J2 pin1 /PIN1. All listed? Need check all pins. For J1/J2 nets: +3V3 pins 11, +5V 27, /BAT 29, GND pins 2,4,6, etc. Need ensure same for both. Netlist includes J1/J2 for most. But some? Let's list:
J1 pins:

Yes.

J3 servo header: pin1 GND, pin2 Net D2-K (servo power), pin3 Net-(J3-Pin_3) with R3 pin1 and R13 pin2. Good.
J8 similar: pin1 GND, pin2 servo power, pin3 Net-(J8-Pin_3) with R4 pin1, R13 pin1, R14 pin2. Good. Wait R13 between J8 pin3 and J3 pin3. R14 between /TTL and J8 pin3. So if R13, R14 shorted: J3 pin3 connected to J8 pin3 and to TTL. But R13 connects J3 pin3 to J8 pin3; R14 connects TTL to J8 pin3. So both bridged. Yes.

R9-R12 mapping. Spec says R9-R12 select which M5Stack bus pin (pin 19/21 for ch.1, pin 20/22 for ch.2) supplies PWM1/PWM2 — schematic note: "Short R10, R10 for Core2 and CoreS3 / Short R9, R11 for others" (typo? maybe R10,R12? Spec says Short R10, R10 for Core2 and CoreS3 / Short R9, R11 for others). Netlist:
/PWM1 net has R10 pin1, R3 pin2, R9 pin1. /PWM1_C1 (pin19) has R9 pin2. /PWM1_C2 (pin21) has R10 pin2. So R9 connects pin19 to PWM1; R10 connects pin21 to PWM1.
/PWM2 net has R11 pin1, R12 pin1, R4 pin2. /PWM2_C1 (pin20) has R11 pin2. /PWM2_C2 (pin22) has R12 pin2. So R11 connects pin20 to PWM2; R12 connects pin22 to PWM2.
Spec says pin 19/21 for ch1, pin20/22 for ch2. Short R9,R11 for others? R9 -> pin19, R11 -> pin20. Core2/CoreS3? "Short R10, R10" likely typo for R10,R12? R10 -> pin21, R12 -> pin22. So yes.

R3, R4 1k series from PWM1/PWM2 to J3/J8 pin3. R3 pin2 /PWM1, pin1 J3. R4 pin2 /PWM2, pin1 J8. Good.
R13/R14 0Ω jumpers. R13 pin2 J3, pin1 J8. R14 pin1 TTL, pin2 J8. Good.
R6 2k +3V3 to /TTL (U1 A). R7 20k from Q2-C to GND? Net Q2-C has R7 pin1, U1 pins 2,3, Q2 pin3. R7 pin2 GND. R8 2.2k +3V3 to U1 B. R15 2.2k U1 B to GND. Bias.
R1 10k +3V3 to /TXD2. R2 5.1k /TXD2 to Q2 base. Q2 emitter +3V3, collector Q2-C. This is PNP: emitter to 3V3, base via R2 from TXD2, R1 pull-up to 3V3. Collector to DE/RE with R7 20k pulldown. Hmm let's analyze: PNP with emitter +3V3, base tied to TXD2 via 5.1k and pull-up 10k. When TXD2 high (3.3V), base-emitter ~0 -> PNP off, collector pulled low by R7 20k, so DE/RE low, receiver enabled, driver disabled. When TXD2 low (0V), base pulled low through R2, PNP on, collector high ~3.3, DE/RE high, driver enabled. That seems auto direction: idle TX high -> receive; transmitting low start bit -> drive. Good. But R7 20k pulldown is heavy? Q2 collector current maybe (3.3 - Vce)/20k = 0.165mA, fine. Actually R7 from Q2-C to GND pulls low when off. Good. Spec says R6, R7, R8, R15 2k,20k,2.2k,2.2k bias/pull network. Yes.

Q1: IRLML6402 P-MOSFET high-side battery disconnect. Net: J5 pin1 to Q1 S (pin2) and R5 pin2. Q1 D (pin3) to /BAT. Q1 G (pin1) to R5 pin1 and SW1 pin2. SW1 pin3 GND, pin1 unconnected. R5 between gate and source. Wait spec says "SW1 SPDT switch; pulls Q1's gate low (via R5, 47k) to turn the battery path on." Let's analyze netlist. Q1 is P-FET. Source at J5 pin1 (battery positive? likely), drain /BAT. Gate net Net-(Q1-G) with R5 pin1 and SW1 pin2. R5 pin2 to J5 pin1/source. SW1 pin3 GND. SW1 pin2 common B. SW1 pin1 unconnected. If switch in one position, pin2-pin3 closed to GND: gate pulled low, P-FET on. If other, pin2-pin1 open: gate pulled to source via R5, off. So yes. But wait R5 is 47k, between gate and source. Good. However spec says "gates the battery connector (J5) onto the /BAT bus net." Q1 source on J5 pin1, drain /BAT. Body diode orientation? For P-FET high-side, source usually to load? Let's think. P-channel MOSFET high-side switch: source connected to input supply (battery positive), drain to load. Gate low turns on. Body diode from drain to source? For P-MOSFET body diode anode at drain, cathode at source? Actually P-channel body diode conducts from drain to source when drain higher than source? In SOT-23 P-FET, source is pin2? IRLML6402 pinout: pin1 G, pin2 S, pin3 D. Body diode from D to S? For P-channel, body diode anode at D, cathode at S. If source at battery, drain at load, body diode from drain (anode) to source (cathode) would conduct if load > battery. That's typical for reverse polarity protection? Wait for high-side P-FET switch, source to supply, drain to load; body diode is reverse-biased when supply positive and load lower. Good. So okay.

But need check Q1 gate drive: R5 between gate and source, SW1 to GND. When SW1 closed, gate pulled to GND through switch. R5 47k and switch. Gate-source voltage = -Vbat, turns on. Good.

J5: pin2 GND, pin1 Q1 source. Good.

J6 PortB: pin1 GND, pin2 +5V, pin3 /PORTB1, pin4 /PORTB2. Good.

J7: pin2 GND, pin1 D1 A. Good.

Now possible anomaly: C3 pin1 on servo rail, pin2 GND; C1,C2,C4 pin1 GND, pin2 rail. All non-polarized. Fine.

Potential issue in SPICE? It lists R6 +3V3 /TTL 2k, R8 +3V3 Net-_U1-B_ 2.2k, R15 Net-_U1-B_ 0 2.2k. Good. R7 Net-_Q2-C_ 0 20k. Good. But no R1? It has R1 +3V3 /TXD2 10k. Yes. V_3V3 only source; no +5V. Spice omits connectors etc. Fine.

Need look for deviations from spec. Let's compare component values/footprints. All match? Let's systematically check each.

Spec table:
J1/J2 Conn_02x15_Odd_Even labelled M-BUS. Netlist J1 footprint PinHeader 2x15 vertical SMD, J2 PinSocket 2x15 vertical SMD. Value Conn_02x15_Odd_Even. Good.
J3, J8 Conn_01x03. Footprint JST EH B3B-EH-A. Good.
J5 Conn_01x02 labelled BAT. JST PH. Good.
J6 Conn_01x04 M5Unit PortB breakout. JST PH 4-pin horizontal. Good.
J7 Conn_01x02 labelled 5V_POWER. JST XH. Good.
D1 SS54 5A Schottky. Footprint D_SMA. LCSC C2931790 maybe SS54? Good.
D2 PMEG3030EP Schottky, 3A 360mV. Footprint SOD-128. LCSC C255587. Good.
C1-C4 100u x4. 1206 hand solder. LCSC C15008. Good.
C5 0.1u 0603. Good.
Q1 IRLML6402 P-ch. SOT-23. Good.
SW1 SPDT. Footprint CuK OS102011MA1QN1 SPDT angled. Good.
Q2 BC857 PNP. SOT-23. Good.
U1 MAX3485. SO-8. Good.
R1 10k, R2 5.1k, R6 2k, R7 20k, R8 2.2k, R15 2.2k. Good.
R3, R4 1k. Good.
R5 47k. Spec says 47k. Good. Note tolerance field 0.1% maybe okay, not anomaly.
R9-R12 0Ω. R13,R14 0Ω. Good.

Potential issue: Q2 PNP base drive. R1 10k pull-up from /TXD2 to +3V3, R2 5.1k to base. This means when TXD2 high, base voltage = 3.3 * 5.1/(10+5.1)? Wait R1 between +3V3 and /TXD2, R2 between /TXD2 and base. The base is not directly tied to TXD2? Let's redraw: +3V3 -- R1 -- /TXD2 -- R2 -- Q2 base. Q2 emitter +3V3. So base is driven through R2 from TXD2, and R1 pulls TXD2 up. This is odd: TXD2 is UART TX output from M5Stack, likely push-pull. R1 pull-up to 3.3 is okay. When TXD2 high, base pulled to high through R2? Actually /TXD2 node high (3.3) through R1? If TXD2 output high, node at 3.3. Base = 3.3 (through R2, no current). Emitter 3.3, Vbe=0, PNP off. When TXD2 low, node low (0), base = 0 through R2? But R1 pulls node up to 3.3; TXD2 output low sinks current through R1 (0.33mA), node near 0. Base near 0, Vbe=-3.3, PNP on. Good. R1 not strictly needed but ensures high. R2 limits base current. Okay.

But check Q2 collector to U1 DE/RE and R7 pulldown. When PNP on, collector pulled to emitter 3.3. But U1 VCC is +3V3. DE high enables driver. When PNP off, R7 pulls DE/RE low. Good. However MAX3485 has active-low RE and active-high DE tied together. When DE/RE low, driver disabled, receiver enabled. When high, driver enabled, receiver disabled. This auto-direction works if TX line idle high. Good.

Potential issue: R6 2k pull-up on A (/TTL) to +3V3, R8/R15 divider on B. For half-duplex RS-485 fail-safe biasing, A should be pulled high, B pulled low. Here A pulled to +3V3 via R6, B pulled to +3V3 via R8 and to GND via R15 (2.2k/2.2k -> 1.65V). Wait standard RS-485 idle/fail-safe: A (non-inverting) should be high, B (inverting) low, differential > 200mV. Here R6 2k pulls A to 3.3, R8/R15 pulls B to 1.65. So A-B = 1.65V. That's fail-safe. R7 20k pulldown on DE/RE? No, R7 on Q2-C to GND, not A/B. R6/R8/R15 yes. Spec says R6, R7, R8, R15 2k, 20k, 2.2k, 2.2k bias/pull network on A/B and DE/RE. R7 20k on DE/RE. Good.

Potential issue: U1 MAX3485 A/B pins? In MAX3485, pin6 A (non-inverting), pin7 B (inverting). Net /TTL connects to A and R6 pull-up; B connects R8 pull-up and R15 pull-down. Good. Servo bus single-wire TTL? Wait MAX3485 is RS-485 differential transceiver. The design spec says it converts UART to shared single-wire TTL serial bus. How is a differential RS-485 transceiver used for single-wire TTL? It says "TTL serial bus" driven through MAX3485 RS-485/RS-422 transceiver. In netlist, U1 A (pin6) is connected to /TTL, and U1 B (pin7) is connected to Net-(U1-B) with R8/R15, not to /TTL. Wait if using MAX3485 for single-wire half-duplex, you'd usually tie A and B? Or use A as single-ended? Let's examine. The spec says "two servo signal pins are bridged into one shared half-duplex TTL serial bus, driven through a MAX3485 RS-485/RS-422 transceiver". It also says R6, R7, R8, R15 bias/pull network on MAX3485 A/B differential lines. The netlist has /TTL connected to R14 (to servo headers) and R6 (pull-up) and U1 A. U1 B has R8 pull-up and R15 pull-down, but is NOT connected to /TTL or servo. That seems suspicious: If B is not connected to the single-wire bus, what's the point? MAX3485 is differential; driver output between A and B. Receiver input between A and B. If B is only biased to 1.65V, and A is connected to the bus (TTL), then when driver enabled, A will be driven relative to B? Actually MAX3485 driver differential output: A and B are complementary. If B is not connected to bus, the bus sees only A toggling relative to local B? Wait the receiver at servo? Serial servos use single-wire half-duplex TTL (like Dynamixel) where signal line is bidirectional, idle high, pulled up. They are not RS-485 differential. To interface MAX3485 to single-wire TTL, there are known circuits: connect A (or B) to the single wire, and set the other line to a reference? Hmm let's think.

MAX3485 driver: differential outputs A and B. When DI high, A high, B low. When DI low, A low, B high. If you connect only A to the single-wire bus and leave B biased at mid, the bus signal will be A (0 to 3.3) relative to ground. The servo reads single-ended TTL. The driver's B output is not connected, so the differential pair is not properly terminated, but the driver still drives A. However the driver output A depends on B? It is a differential output with internal transistors; if B unloaded, A can still swing. But for the receiver, MAX3485's RO depends on (A-B). If B is fixed at 1.65V, and A is the bus signal (idle high ~3.3, low ~0), then A-B: idle 1.65V -> RO high? Actually for RS-485, if A > B by >200mV, RO high (idle mark). If A < B by < -200mV, RO low. So when bus idle high 3.3, A-B=1.65 -> RO high. When servo drives bus low 0, A-B=-1.65 -> RO low. That works as single-ended receiver with B mid-supply. So B biased to mid via R8/R15 is intentional! R6 pulls A high to fail-safe idle. So the MAX3485 is used in a pseudo-single-ended mode: A is the bus, B is biased at mid. That matches spec? The spec says "bias/pull network on the MAX3485 A/B differential lines" and "shared single-wire TTL serial bus". It doesn't explicitly say B connected to bus. But the schematic likely does this. Need check if this is intended? Let's examine R6, R8, R15: R6 2k from +3V3 to A (/TTL). R8 2.2k from +3V3 to B. R15 2.2k from B to GND. So B at 1.65V. A is pulled high but can be driven by bus. That's a known "single-wire RS-485 to TTL" trick? Actually to connect a MAX3485 to a single-wire half-duplex bus, you often tie A and B together? Wait if A and B tied together, differential voltage zero, receiver output indeterminate. Not good. Or use A for data and B for inverted data? For half-duplex single-wire, you might connect A to bus and B to a reference voltage (Vcc/2). Yes, some designs use that. So not anomaly.

But wait the spec says "the two servo signal pins are bridged into one shared half-duplex TTL serial bus, driven through a MAX3485 RS-485/RS-422 transceiver". It also says "U1 MAX3485 (half-duplex RS-485/RS-422 transceiver) Converts the M5Stack's UART (TXD2/RXD2, PortC) to the shared single-wire TTL serial servo bus." It doesn't mention B bias in detail. The netlist is likely correct reference. Need find actual anomaly inserted.

Let's check for subtle tampering. Compare netlist to spec. Potential anomalies:
- R1 and R2 values swapped? Spec says R1 10k, R2 5.1k. Netlist matches. But let's analyze if R1 10k pull-up and R2 5.1k base is correct? Yes.
- Q2 PNP base: maybe R1 should be between TXD2 and base, R2 pull-up? Spec says "driven from /TXD2 (via R1 10k, R2 5.1k) to toggle..." Not precise. Netlist: R1 from +3V3 to /TXD2; R2 from /TXD2 to base. That's a voltage divider? Wait if R1 is pull-up on TXD2, R2 series to base. That's plausible. But if R1 is pull-up and R2 series, when TXD2 low, base current = (3.3 - Vbe)/(R1+R2?) Actually current path from +3V3 through R1 into TXD2 low? Wait TXD2 is driven low by MCU. The node /TXD2 is low (0V). R1 from +3V3 to node draws current through R1 to MCU. R2 from node to base: base at ~0.7V? Let's calculate: Node /TXD2 is held low by MCU (push-pull). So node ≈ 0V. Base is connected via R2 to node. Emitter at 3.3. Base-emitter junction forward biased, base voltage ~2.6V (3.3 - 0.7). But node is 0V. So current flows from emitter through base-emitter junction, through R2 to node, then into MCU low. That means base current = (2.6V - 0V)/5.1k ≈ 0.51mA. Actually the base is not at 0; it's at Vbe below emitter. Wait Q2 emitter at +3V3, base connected via R2 to /TXD2 (0V). The base-emitter junction is a diode from base to emitter? For PNP, emitter is P, base is N. Forward bias means base is lower than emitter by Vbe (~0.7), so base voltage = 2.6V. Current flows from emitter to base to R2 to node. Yes. R1 from +3V3 to /TXD2 (node) draws additional current (3.3V/10k=0.33mA) from +3V3 into MCU low. That's fine. When TXD2 high (3.3V), node = 3.3V, base via R2 = 3.3V, Vbe=0, off. R1 no current. So R1 is a pull-up to ensure node high if TXD2 is open-drain? But UART TX is push-pull. R1 maybe unnecessary but okay. However R1 10k from +3V3 to /TXD2 means when TXD2 is low, it adds 0.33mA load. Not issue. R2 5.1k base current ~0.5mA, enough for Q2? Q2 collector current ~0.165mA, so fine.

Wait, if R1 were in series with base and R2 pull-up, would be different. But netlist matches spec? Spec: "Q2 | BC857 (PNP) | Auto TX/RX direction-control transistor: driven from /TXD2 (via R1 10k, R2 5.1k) to toggle..." "R1, R2 | 10k, 5.1k | Bias/divider from /TXD2 into Q2's base." The netlist: R1 +3V3 to /TXD2, R2 /TXD2 to base. That's not a divider from /TXD2 into base? Actually it's R1 pull-up on /TXD2 and R2 series into base. But spec says "Bias/divider from /TXD2 into Q2's base." Could be interpreted as R1/R2 forming divider? Hmm if R1 from +3V3 to /TXD2 and R2 from /TXD2 to base, not a divider from /TXD2 into base; it's a pull-up plus series. But maybe original design has R1 from /TXD2 to base and R2 from base to +3V3? Let's think standard auto-direction circuit for MAX3485 using PNP: Usually TXD connects to base via resistor, emitter to Vcc, collector to DE/RE, with pull-down on DE/RE. Sometimes a pull-up on TXD. Spec says R1 10k, R2 5.1k. Which is which? Netlist has R1 10k +3V3 to /TXD2, R2 5.1k /TXD2 to base. Could be correct if R1 is pull-up and R2 base resistor. But spec says "R1, R2 | 10k, 5.1k | Bias/divider from /TXD2 into Q2's base." That could match either. Not enough.

Let's check other possible anomalies. Look at U1 pin connections. MAX3485 pinout:
1 RO -> /RXD2 (J1/J2 pin16)
2 ~RE -> Net-(Q2-C) with R7, DE
3 DE -> same
4 DI -> /TXD2
5 GND
6 A -> /TTL
7 B -> Net-(U1-B) with R8/R15
8 VCC -> +3V3
This is correct for half-duplex with auto direction.

But wait: For MAX3485, receiver output RO is connected to /RXD2. When driver enabled (DE high), receiver disabled (~RE high). When driver disabled (DE low), receiver enabled. Good.

Potential issue: R7 20k on DE/RE to GND. When Q2 on, collector pulls high. But Q2 collector is PNP collector; when on, it can source current from emitter to collector. The collector voltage will be close to emitter (3.3) minus Vce(sat). R7 20k pulls down. Good. When Q2 off, R7 pulls DE/RE low. Good.

Potential issue: Q2 emitter tied to +3V3, base driven from /TXD2 which is also 3.3V logic. When TXD2 high, PNP off. When TXD2 low, PNP on. This inverts TXD: during start bit (low), driver enabled. But during idle high, receiver enabled. That's standard. However the driver's DI is connected directly to /TXD2. When driver enabled, DI low -> driver drives A low, B high. When idle high, driver disabled, receiver enabled. But the bus is single-wire; when driver disabled, the MAX3485's A output is high-impedance? Actually driver disabled, receiver enabled, so A is input. But R6 pulls A high. Good. Servo can drive bus. The M5Stack's TXD2 is also connected to DI and to Q2 base. When servo responds, bus signal goes to A, receiver outputs to RO (/RXD2). But TXD2 is still driven by M5Stack UART. If M5Stack UART is not transmitting, TXD2 idle high. That's fine. But if M5Stack UART is idle high, Q2 off, receiver enabled. If servo drives bus, receiver output RO drives /RXD2. But /RXD2 is connected to M5Stack RXD2 input, and also to U1 RO output. That's fine. However M5Stack TXD2 output is also connected to U1 DI and Q2 base; no conflict.

Wait: /RXD2 net has J1 pin16, J2 pin16, U1 pin1 RO. But is there any pull-up? No. MAX3485 RO is push-pull output. Fine.

Potential issue: D1 and D2 orientation. D1: J7 pin1 -> anode, cathode -> +5V. That means external 5V input can feed +5V through D1. But spec says "diode-isolated from M5Stack 5V rail" and "blocks backfeed from the +5V rail out through the external-power jack". Yes. D2: +5V -> anode, cathode -> servo rail. Good. However check D1 part: SS54 is Schottky, forward voltage >0.6V. D2 PMEG3030EP 3A 360mV. Good.

Potential issue: C1-C4 100u on servo rail. Check C3 pin orientation: C3 pin1 on Net-(D2-K), pin2 GND. Others pin2 on Net, pin1 GND. Non-polarized. Fine.

Potential issue: J1/J2 pass-through. Spec says "identical nets on both so the board can be stacked between the M5Stack Core and a lower module (pass-through). Carries +5V, +3V3, BAT, GND, GPIO/UART pins (TXD2/RXD2 = PortC UART, two PortB GPIOs) through to J6." Netlist has J6 on +5V, GND, /PORTB1, /PORTB2. But note J1/J2 pins 3 and 9 are /PORTB2 and /PORTB1, respectively. Spec says J6 carries GND, +5V, two GPIOs (/PORTB1, /PORTB2) through from J1/J2. Netlist: J6 pin1 GND, pin2 +5V, pin3 /PORTB1 (J1/J2 pin9), pin4 /PORTB2 (J1/J2 pin3). Good.

Potential issue: J1/J2 pin assignments for M5Stack bus. Need verify against M5Stack M-BUS pinout? Spec doesn't list exact pin numbers except some. It says J1/J2 pins 19/21 for ch1, 20/22 for ch2, 15/16 TXD2/RXD2, 27 +5V, 29 BAT. Netlist matches. But maybe there is a swapped pin: /PWM2_C1 is J1/J2 pin20, /PWM2_C2 pin22. Spec says "pin 20/22 for ch.2". Good. /PWM1_C1 pin19, /PWM1_C2 pin21. Good.

Potential issue: R9-R12 jumpers. Spec says "Short R10, R10 for Core2 and CoreS3 / Short R9, R11 for others" (typo). Netlist has R9 connects /PWM1 to /PWM1_C1 (pin19), R10 connects /PWM1 to /PWM1_C2 (pin21), R11 connects /PWM2 to /PWM2_C1 (pin20), R12 connects /PWM2 to /PWM2_C2 (pin22). So for "others" short R9, R11 -> ch1 pin19, ch2 pin20. For Core2/CoreS3 short R10, R12 -> ch1 pin21, ch2 pin22. Spec says "Short R10, R10" maybe typo for R10, R12. But netlist has R12 present. So okay.

Potential issue: The spec says "R3, R4 1k each Series resistors from PWM1/PWM2 GPIO nets to J3 pin 3 / J8 pin 3 respectively." Netlist: R3 pin2 /PWM1, pin1 J3. R4 pin2 /PWM2, pin1 J8. Good.

Potential issue: "R13, R14 0 Ω (jumpers) When shorted, bridge J3-pin3 and J8-pin3 together and onto the MAX3485 TTL bus". Netlist: R13 between J3 pin3 and J8 pin3; R14 between TTL and J8 pin3. So if both shorted, all connected. Good.

Wait, let's get body diode direction correct.

P-channel MOSFET body diode: The substrate is N-type, source and drain are P+. The body is connected to source. The PN junction between drain (P) and body (N) forms a diode with anode at drain (P) and cathode at body/source (N). So diode conducts from drain to source when drain is more positive than source by ~0.7V. Yes, anode at drain, cathode at source. So current flows drain -> source when drain > source.

For high-side switch off, we want no current from battery to load or load to battery. If source is battery, drain is load: diode conducts from load to battery when load > battery. So if load (e.g., M5Stack BAT with USB charging) > battery, current flows from load to battery. That means external battery can be charged even when switch off. If source is load (/BAT), drain is battery: diode conducts from battery to load when battery > load. That means battery can discharge to load even when switch off. Neither orientation blocks both directions. To block both directions, you need two back-to-back MOSFETs or a MOSFET with body diode oriented to block the undesired direction. In a simple high-side switch, you usually orient source to input, drain to load. When off, body diode is reverse-biased for the normal input-to-output direction? Wait, if source is input (battery), drain is load, and battery > load, then drain < source, so diode is reverse-biased (anode at drain lower than cathode source). So no conduction from battery to load. But if load > battery, diode conducts from load to battery. So it blocks battery-to-load when off, but not load-to-battery. That's typical: it disconnects the battery from the load, but if the load is driven higher by another source, it can feed back. In this design, the /BAT net is connected to M5Stack BAT pin. If USB power is present, the M5Stack's charger may raise /BAT to ~4.2V, which is higher than external battery (say 3.7V), so current could flow from /BAT to external battery through Q1 body diode, charging it. If the switch is off, the external battery should be disconnected from the M5Stack, but the M5Stack can still charge it? That might be a known limitation. The spec says "High-side battery disconnect switch: gates the battery connector (J5) onto the /BAT bus net." It doesn't mention reverse blocking. So likely reference design.

P-channel MOSFET body diode: The substrate is N-type, source and drain are P+. The body is connected to source.
